subject: Error fitting simple models with rw1 component using pardiso solver

messages.author: 59e3bac9cafb3a9b
messages.subject: Error fitting simple models with rw1 component using pardiso solver
parts:
Dear INLA users,

I am trying to fit models of increasing complexity with the pardiso solver (& valid license) on a dataset of 34664 observations.
However, fitting even simpler models such as  "NoPerHaul ~ Survey + f(Year, model = 'rw1') + offset(logSweptAreakm2)") result in the following error:

inla.mkl: smtp-pardiso.c:757: GMRFLib_pardiso_solve_core: Assertion \`store-\>pstore-\>done_with_chol == GMRFLib_TRUE' failed.

I tried to impelment the advice from the following conversation to check if a lack of Memory is the problem, but so far I have not managed to resolve the issue:
https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/fDi_BRZflr4/m/iasLoxZrBAAJ.

Do you have any sugggestions how to go about tryting to resolve this error?

I attached the notebook with the code and data.

Regards,
Timo Staeudle

Below some further details to the system and attempts to solve the issue:

Linux server details: PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)" NAME="Debian GNU/Linux" VERSION_ID="11" VERSION="11 (bullseye)" VERSION_CODENAME=bullseye ID=debian HOME_URL="<https://www.debian.org/>" SUPPORT_URL="<https://www.debian.org/support>" BUG_REPORT_URL="<https://bugs.debian.org/>"

Memory: - Memory availability: \>200Gb (server total 376Gb)
Cores: 72

R-INLA version ..........: 21.02.23

Further details & unsuccessful attempts so far:

-   smtp = "taucs" fits the INLA model with as.formula( "... + f(Year, model = 'rw1')")

-   when setting openmp.strategy="pardiso" model does not fit data if considering year as a random effect "... + f(Year, model = 'rw1')"  -> this seems to be specific to "rw1" random effects

Unsuccessful attempts to solve this error when attempting to fit model using openmp.strategy="pardiso":
- remove config = T
- setting control.inla = list(strategy = "adaptive", int.strategy = "eb")
- trying to reduce reduce memory by setting: num.threads = "2:-1" (as we have currently 2 hyperparameters) 
- reducing number of observations by setting data = sample_frac(data, 0.4) does fit the model on the subset.
